goal: Triage large log files and log directories using Recursive Language Model (RLM) decomposition: cluster errors…
use: Triage large log files and log directories using Recursive Language Model (RLM) decomposition: cluster errors by signature, count and date them, and rank likely root causes with evidence. Use when asked to investigate an incident, find the cause of errors, or summarize logs too large to read in one pass.

steps.note: Scope the incident. Ask for the time window, the service, and the symptom if they are not given.
Map. For each chunk, run a fresh sub-task (a subagent if you can start one) that sees the chunk and the "Chunk task" below.
Verify. Open each cited file and line, confirm each finding against the source, and drop any finding you cannot confirm.

protocol.title: Scope the incident
protocol.text: Ask for the time window, the service, and the symptom if they are not given. Narrow the files to that window before chunking.

protocol.title: Inspect
protocol.text: Run `python3 <skill>/scripts/rlm_corpus.py scan <logs> --include '*.log' --include '*.txt' --max-bytes 52428800`. Note the file sizes and skipped files. Compressed logs (`.gz`) are not read: decompress the window you need into a work folder first.

protocol.title: Map
protocol.text: For each chunk, run a fresh sub-task (a subagent if you can start one) that sees the chunk and the "Chunk task" below. If you cannot start sub-tasks, run `python3 <skill>/scripts/rlm_corpus.py pending "$WORK/chunks" "$WORK/out"` and process the first listed chunk, then run `pending` again until nothing is pending.

protocol.title: Reduce
protocol.text: Run `python3 <skill>/scripts/rlm_corpus.py merge "$WORK/out" --out "$WORK/merged.json"`. Re-run any `failed_outputs`. Group the merged items by their `finding` signature, then count them.

protocol.title: Verify
protocol.text: Open each cited file and line, confirm each finding against the source, and drop any finding you cannot confirm.

protocol.title: Trace
protocol.text: For the top clusters, open the log lines around the first occurrence and confirm the sequence that led to it. Look for the first error in a request or correlation ID, not only the most frequent one.

protocol.title: Report
protocol.text: Write the report in the format below.

protocol.title: Clean up
protocol.text: Delete `$WORK` after the report is delivered.
